items.q: What is a vector?
items.a: A quantity with magnitude and direction
hints: Recall the defining property of a vector, as opposed to a scalar.
A vector has both a size and a direction, unlike a scalar which only has size.
A quantity with magnitude and direction

items.q: Can the magnitude of a vector be negative?
hints: Magnitude is a length — think about what kind of quantity a length is.
A length can never be negative, so neither can |a|.
No

items.q: Are vectors with the same magnitude and direction equal?
hints: Recall what makes two vectors identical.
Vectors are defined purely by magnitude and direction, not by position.
Yes

items.q: What symbol is often used to describe the magnitude of vector a?
hints: Recall the standard notation for 'size of' a vector.
Vertical bars around the vector represent its magnitude.

items.q: Does direction matter for vectors?
hints: Compare a vector to a scalar.
Unlike a scalar, a vector always carries a direction as well as a size.
Yes

items.q: True or false: vectors can represent displacement.
hints: Think about a real-world quantity that has both size and direction.
Displacement has a distance (magnitude) and a direction, so it is a vector.
True

items.q: Find the magnitude of the vector (3,4).
hints: Use Pythagoras: magnitude = sqrt(x-component^2 + y-component^2).

items.q: If a = (2,3) and b = (5,-1), find a + b.
hints: Add column vectors component by component.

items.q: If a = (2,3) and b = (5,-1), find a - b.
hints: Subtract column vectors component by component.

items.q: If a = (2,3), find 2a.
hints: Multiply every component of the vector by the scalar.

items.q: If p = (1,4) and q = (-2,3), find p + q.
hints: Add column vectors component by component.

items.q: If p = (1,4) and q = (-2,3), find p - q.
hints: Subtract column vectors component by component.

items.q: If a = (3,-2) and b = (1,5), find 2a + b.
hints: Scale the first vector, then add the second component by component.

items.q: Complete: AB + BC = ?
hints: Think of AB and BC as consecutive journeys — where do they end up starting and finishing?
Travelling A to B then B to C is the same as travelling directly A to C.
AC

items.q: In a parallelogram, vector AB equals which opposite side vector?
hints: In parallelogram ABCD, opposite sides are parallel and equal in length and direction.
AB and DC point the same way round the parallelogram.
DC

items.q: If P divides AB in the ratio 1:2, which point is closer to A or B?
hints: The ratio AP:PB tells you how the segment is split — compare the two parts.
AP:PB = 1:2 means AP is the smaller part.
A

items.q: True or false: vector proofs rely on direction as well as length.
hints: Recall what distinguishes a vector from a plain length.
Vector proofs must track both magnitude and direction throughout.
True

items.q: What law states AB + BC = AC?
hints: Recall the name of the rule for adding vectors head-to-tail.
Adding two vectors that form two sides of a triangle gives the third side — this is the triangle law.
Triangle law

items.q: In a parallelogram, vector AD equals which opposite side vector?
hints: In parallelogram ABCD, opposite sides are parallel and equal in length and direction.
AD and BC point the same way round the parallelogram.
BC

items.q: In triangle OAB, M is the midpoint of AB. Given OA = a and OB = b, express OM in terms of a and b.
hints: Write OM as OA plus half of AB, then express AB in terms of a and b.
AB = OB - OA = b - a, so OM = a + (1/2)(b - a).
